basis: Cobalamin metabolic defect defined by megaloblastic anemia and encephalopathy; retinopathy occurs in 30-79%.
Thiamine-deficiency brain injury causes encephalopathy and amnesia; abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Fatty acid/amino acid oxidation disorder; myopathy with proximal weakness and elevated CK occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and hepatic injury are minority features across the umbrella.
Carcinoma originates in the rectum; sarcomatoid differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Primary skeletal muscle dystrophy with contractures. Respiratory insufficiency in 60% reflects muscle weakness; cardiac disease is reported in under 30%.
Benign chondroid-producing tumor arising in bone, usually the epiphysis of a long bone.
Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis; stroke occurs in only 5/64 patients.
Congenital viral injury chiefly affects the developing brain; destructive retinal/macular lesions are defining features and occur in roughly 30-50% of syndromic cases.
Portal vascular hypertension; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia in 2/5 and hypersplenism with thrombocytopenia in 8/9. Esophageal varices are vascular lesions.
Occupational cotton-dust airway and lung disease; no established autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Vaginal discharge is confined to the reproductive tract; an infectious cause is not established by this concept.
Structural aortic valve displacement with possible valvular regurgitation.
Premature red-cell destruction defines the disease; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Mechanical compression obstructs the duodenum; the adjacent arteries are not themselves diseased or damaged.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and epileptic spasms define the disorder; persistent esotropia reported in 1/2 patients supports ocular involvement, with a very small sample.
Radio-digital dysplasia indicates skeletal malformation; absent definition and phenotype data prevent reliable assignment of additional organs.
Inflammatory disease of the choroid, retina and vitreous, usually infectious or immune-mediated.
Cardiac and skeletal malformations define Noonan syndrome; ptosis in 77/136 and bleeding tendency with bruising in 32/56 support ocular and hematologic involvement. ID is under 30%.
Endotoxin-triggered inflammatory small-vessel injury with intravascular coagulation, thrombosis and hemorrhagic necrosis.
Malignant tumor originates in the tongue, an oral cavity structure; sensory-system ancestry does not establish neurologic involvement.
Gonadal endocrine failure and sensorimotor peripheral nerve loss define the syndrome. Muscle wasting is neurogenic rather than primary muscle disease.
Tapeworm infection occupies the small intestine; anemia and other extraintestinal damage are not established as common.
Developmental impairment and hand/foot skeletal malformations characterize the syndrome; ocular malformations are variable without evidence establishing a frequency of at least 30%.
Hereditary apolipoprotein misfolding and amyloid deposition predominantly cause progressive renal disease; common functional injury elsewhere is not established.
Anaerobic bacterial infection of the glans penis; the reproductive site has no dedicated organ axis.
